content: We need to determine if the assistant's response (the tool calls) contains a contextual error according to policy. The response includes four tool calls in one turn: update_reservation_flights for NM1VX1, update_reservation_flights for H8Q05L, cancel_reservation for KC18K6, cancel_reservation for S61CZX. According to policy, before taking any actions that update the booking database (modifying flights, cancelling reservations), must list action details and obtain explicit user confirmation (yes) to proceed. The user did confirm: they said "Итак, я подтверждаю: — Повышение класса до бизнес для NM1VX1 и H8Q05L с оплатой картой Visa. — Отмену бронирований KC18K6 и S61CZX." That is explicit confirmation. However, the policy also says: "You should only make one tool call at a time, and if you make a tool call, you should not respond to the user simultaneously. If you respond to the user, you should not make a tool call at the same time." The assistant made multiple tool calls in a single turn (four). That violates the rule of only one tool call at a time. Also, they didn't list action details before making the calls. They did list details earlier in the conversation, but the policy says before taking any actions that update the booking database, you must list the action details and obtain explicit user confirmation. The assistant listed details in previous turns (they gave cost breakdown etc.) and got confirmation. However, they didn't list the specific action details (like "I will update reservation NM1VX1 to business class, etc.") right before the calls. But they did earlier. The policy likely expects that before each action, you list details and get confirmation. The user gave a blanket confirmation for all actions
